description: A geometry library for engineering drawings and models, in two dimensions and in three. Points, vectors, lines, polylines, polygons, faces with holes, circles and oriented rectangles in the plane; points, planes, triangles, polygons, faces, solids, boxes, coordinate systems and transformations in space. Over both: distance, projection, containment, intersection, collision, parallelism, parametrization, merging, splitting, extending and trimming, offsetting, and boolean operations. It also carries the label placement that arranges drawing labels clear of each other and of blocked regions, and packs boxes such as drawing views onto sheets of paper. Every comparison is tolerance-aware, because coordinates that come out of a BIM model are never exact.
releaseNotes:
NEW IN 12.2.0

      NEW, the ray in the plane
      - GeoRay2, an origin and a direction it runs along for ever, the counterpart of GeoRay3. It is asked what a
        segment is asked, against every shape in the plane, and every shape that takes a GeoLine2 takes a GeoRay2 back.
        PlanarMap.ProjectToRay2/ToRay3, GeoBvh2.GetIntersections and GeoTransform2 take it too.

      FIXED, collisions in the plane read by the tolerance everywhere
      - Two shapes in the plane collide exactly where they come within the point tolerance of each other: they cross,
        one holds the other, or their boundaries pass within EqualPoint. Segments and rays against open curves, curved
        loops, polygons, rectangles, triangles and faces, and every pair of curves, now read so; distances still give
        the gap, and are nought only where the shapes truly cross or overlap.
      - Two segments no longer collide, nor measure nought, where a crossing lies up to the tolerance past their ends:
        corners 0.00156 apart at 1E-3 are apart. TryIntersectWith still places such a crossing.
      - A segment inside a circle's tangent band gets its true crossings; a curved loop near a chord of a bowed edge is
        read by its true boundary; nearly flat arcs keep their crossings whichever is asked first; tolerance forms read
        the tolerance passed all the way down.
      - Label placement no longer puts a label within the tolerance of a line or region kept clear.

      FIXED, fillets and chamfers
      - A fillet is the arc on the inside of the corner and never runs past it: no more cusps where the radius was
        small against the tolerance. A corner that does not turn is left alone.
      - A fillet or chamfer taking an edge whole, give or take the tolerance, meets its neighbour instead of throwing;
        a chain's end points never move. Corner3, and the Tekla bars and ties built through it, no longer throw on tiny
        bends.
      - A curved chain that drops a repeated vertex keeps the bulge of the edge that still has a length.

      FIXED, offsets
      - Curved offsets keep what stands exactly the distance from the shape: folds are cut where they come nearer,
        closing corners are no longer bridged, an arc whose radius runs out is gone round at its two ends, holes are
        kept however their pieces meet, and the answer no longer depends on the start vertex or direction.
      - Curved offsets join corners as the straight ones do: a chamfer at the distance, a miter squared off at the
        limit. They no longer throw at a coarse tolerance.
      - A straight polyline's offset is its band's edge with no fragments past a sharp corner or lying on the
        polyline, and its pieces are ordered in near-linear time: 10 000 vertices in 0.57 s where it took 36 s.
      - A flat chain in space that encloses no area has its plane; round joins keep within OffsetOptions.ArcTolerance.

      CHANGED
      - Offsetting in a plane in space no longer slows with the square of its edges where neighbouring points are
        counted: 100 000 vertices in 1.0 s where it took 15.9 s. Results are unchanged.
      - Reading a near miss as a collision measures a distance where only a crossing was looked for: such pairs, and
        curved offsets of shapes with a few edges, take up to about twice as long; curved offsets of large shapes are
        many times faster.

      Details in CHANGELOG.md.

      Earlier releases: https://github.com/nguyenthanguth/GeometryHelper/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
